chitchat: Sabbatini listens to something out on the water, decides it is nothing, and goes back to the book.
She turns the desk lamp a few degrees further from her face.
She marks her page with a berth card and squares the book up.
Somewhere east of the glass a hull knocks once against a fender. She does not react.
description: She sits with the desk lamp turned away from her so it lights the counter and not her face, which is either courtesy or preference. Forearms like somebody who used to do a heavier job than this one, and a paperback face down beside the berth book that she does not pick up while you are standing there.

root.text: "Evening." She marks her page. "Buying, hiring, or looking for your own?"

text_by_relation.first:
The woman behind the desk marks her page before she looks up, and looks up properly.

"Sabbatini. I do the desk for hulls." She nods at the berth board. "Buy one, hire one, or ask me where yours is. The dock is east and lit all night, the chandlery is west, and Anchovies is north."
text_by_relation.known: "You keep odd hours." Said without judgement, from a woman on nights. "What does she need?"
text_by_relation.familiar: "Sit down if you like." She does not move the paperback. "What does she need?"

options.label: I want to buy a boat.
How do I take her out?

buy.text: She turns the berth book round. "Everything we sell is on the list. use desk and I will show you the lot, or boat reads it out. boat and a name buys that one." "She comes with a full tank and a berth. I put her in the first free one, and boats tells you where she is from anywhere in the city."

hire.text: She finds a rate card under the paperback. "Any hull on the list, for two hours, at a fraction of the price. boat rent shows the rates and boat rent with a name takes one. One at a time." "When the time is up and she is tied up here, she goes back by herself. boat return hands her back early. No paint or names on a hire."

keep.text: She turns in her chair to the berth board. "Four places to keep her, and you pay for the roof." "East, the Dock Hall: under cover, with the hoist and Marit, and the only berth where a hull comes back fully sound. West, through the chandlery, the Hardstanding: cradles in the open, and the cheapest. North of the Hardstanding, the visitor pontoon and the fuel berth: afloat, alongside." "Stand at a berth and berth reads you the board. berth and her name moves her in, if there is room and she is already in this yard. boats tells you where she is now."

drive.text: "Go on, then." She does not get up. "Go to wherever she is lying and board. That puts you aboard. helm puts you at the wheel, and the controls card comes up the first time." "K is the key, and she will not start with the lever open. From the log, conn start, then conn with a bearing or a bell." "Coming home, stop alongside a berth and disembark. That ties her up. Do it on open water and you are swimming. If she dies out there, tow brings her home, and you settle the bill before she goes out again."

fuel.text: She points north with the paperback. "The fuel berth, on the north face of the building, east along the gangway from the visitor pontoon. It is the only marine pump on the Basin." "Bring her alongside the pylons, stop, and fuel. You pay by the unit, so a bigger tank costs more to fill."

work.text: "Marit Colvane, in the Dock Hall, east. She is in from nine in the morning until six, so not now." "Stand in the hall with her there and refit, and Marit puts the hull back to sound wherever your boat is lying in this yard. Servicing, paint and a name need the boat under the roof: berth her in the hall, or bring her into the covered slot and stop. Then refit service, refit paint or refit name." "Tonight you patch her yourself. Marit sells hull patches when she is in. A patch gets her to about half on the water and most of the way on a cradle."

eat.text: "Anchovies, the north doors." She does not look round. "Ottavia serves from six until midnight. After that the kitchen is shut until the next evening."

bye.text: "Mind how you go on that deck." She is reading again before you turn round.

clothing_layers: a marina fleece worn open over the top of everything else
a thick jersey that predates the job
work trousers with the knees gone pale
boots, laced, on a shift where nobody would check

name: Odile Sabbatini
